conflicts.permit: The type of information that we may collect includes your first and last name, email address, geo-location, password, or other identifying information you choose to provide.
conflicts.prohibit: A name, signature, Social Security number, physical characteristics or description, address, telephone number
conflicts.situation: A California resident registers an account and provides a first and last name; the CCPA notice marks the Customer Records category containing names as not collected.
conflicts.reason: The CCPA table marks the Customer Records category, which lists name and telephone number, as "Collected: No" while the policy collects names. The overlap note does not say which entry governs.

conflicts.permit: We collect device specific information when you access our Services from a mobile device, including your hardware model, operating system and version, unique device identifiers, device software platform and firmware, data about usage of our Services while connected to devices that you authorize us to integrate, geographical data and mobile network information
conflicts.prohibit: We will only collect such information if (a) “location services” for the mobile application is enabled; and (b) the permissions in the mobile device allow communication of this information.
conflicts.situation: A user accesses the Services from a mobile device with location services disabled for the app.
conflicts.reason: The device information section lists geographical data as collected automatically without condition, while the geo-location section limits collection to enabled location services. The policy does not say whether geographical data differs from geo-location.

conflicts.permit: We reserve the right to disclose your information when we believe release is appropriate to comply with the law, judicial proceedings, court order or other legal processes; enforce or apply our Terms of Service and other agreements; or protect the rights, property, or safety of Fun Apps and Games by SCHACH, our employees, our users, or others.
conflicts.prohibit: Should Fun Apps and Games by SCHACH handle non-public or contact information, the information will not be published or disclosed without user's consent.
conflicts.situation: The company receives a court order or legal request for a user's email address or phone number, and the user has not consented to the disclosure.
conflicts.reason: The consent requirement for contact information states no exception for legal disclosures, and section 6.5 does not refer to it. Blanket acceptance of the policy may count as consent, but the policy does not say so.

conflicts.permit: In the event that Fun Apps and Games by SCHACH undergoes a business transition, such as a merger, acquisition by another company, or sale of all or a portion of its assets, we may transfer all of your information, including personal information, to the successor organization in such transition.
conflicts.prohibit: Should Fun Apps and Games by SCHACH handle non-public or contact information, the information will not be published or disclosed without user's consent.
conflicts.situation: The company is acquired and transfers users' contact information to the successor organization without asking the users for consent.
conflicts.reason: The business transfer clause covers all information, including contact information, and the consent requirement states no exception for business transfers. Whether blanket acceptance of the policy counts as consent is not stated.

conflicts.permit: Information collected will vary depending upon the activity or service and may include (but not restricted to) your name, email address, phone number, home address, birth date, Facebook account, friends list, mobile phone number and credit card information.
conflicts.prohibit: Fun Apps and Games by SCHACH does not sell products or in-apps to children and does not knowingly collect personal information from children.
conflicts.situation: A child under 13 registers for a game with a parent's involvement, as section 8 allows, and provides a name and birth date.
conflicts.reason: Section 8 permits children under 13 to use the apps with a parent, which makes collection from them known, but states no exception to the collection described in section 2.1.

conflicts.permit: Analytics, information about what you do in the game, to help use improve the game
conflicts.prohibit: DOES NOT collect internet, search, network activity information
conflicts.situation: A player uses the game while in-game analytics record their actions and device identifiers are used to attribute their actions to ad campaigns.
conflicts.reason: The DOES NOT list mirrors CCPA categories, where network activity includes interaction with an application or advertisement. The policy does not define the term or exclude in-game analytics.

conflicts.permit: We provide our partners with some information about the way you use our app so they can advertise products and services that are more likely to be relevant to you.
conflicts.situation: The app's measuring tools record how a user uses the app, and this usage information is provided to advertising partners.
conflicts.reason: The Analytics section lists both "Only by us" and "By us and our partners" without selecting one, and other sections share usage data with advertisers and ad networks. The policy does not say which applies.

conflicts.permit: We do not ask for consent
conflicts.prohibit: We will ask for your consent when sending messages:
conflicts.situation: The app sends a direct marketing email or in-app message to a user's contacts.
conflicts.reason: The Direct Marketing section states both that consent will be asked when messaging the user or contacts and that consent is not asked, with no condition separating them.

conflicts.prohibit: If we learn that personal information from users less than 18 years of age has been collected, we will deactivate the account and take reasonable measures to promptly delete such data from our records.
conflicts.situation: A parent consents to a 16-year-old's use of the Services, the minor registers, and the company learns the user is under 18.
conflicts.reason: The policy accepts use by minors with parental consent but commits to deactivating and deleting any account of a user under 18, with no exception for parental consent.
